observation_summary: The method createCopy throws an IllegalArgumentException when the calculated range of indices is invalid (specifically when the end index is less than the start index), instead of returning an empty series as expected.
reasoning_summary: The fix adds a missing condition to an existing if-statement that checks for an empty range. The original code only checked if the end index was negative, but failed to account for cases where the end index is valid but smaller than the start index, leading to an exception in the subsequent call to createCopy(startIndex, endIndex). This is a classic case of missing validation logic for input parameters.
evidence_used: The stack trace shows an IllegalArgumentException: 'Requires start <= end.' thrown from TimeSeries.createCopy.
The fix_diff_oracle shows the addition of '|| (endIndex < startIndex)' to the existing 'if (endIndex < 0)' check.
The bug report states: 'Here I would expect an empty serie to be returned, not an exception.'

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix modifies the logic, it is specifically adding a missing validation check to prevent an invalid state from reaching the core logic, which fits the definition of 'Checking' better than 'Algorithm/Method'.
